epistemics.$note: Every value in this document carries a `state`. State drives MATERIAL in the UI. This is the core of the design.

states.observed: measured / reported inventory. Renders as METAL.
states.pledged: promised, projected or extrapolated. Renders as GLASS.
states.unknown: not yet parsed or not published. Renders as UNVERIFIED (hairline outline, no fill).
states.absent: confirmed not to exist. Renders as VOID (machined empty socket).

series.$note: series.observed holds several sources and must not be read as one curve. DS-35: All greenhouse gases including land-use change, GWP100 (OWID, from Climate Watch / PIK), from 1990. DS-02: Asset-level observed emissions, CO₂e GWP100 (Climate TRACE); land use accounted differently from OWID, 2015-2025. DS-40: Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). Non-Annex I Parties report only the years their national communications cover, and the figure is negative where reported removals exceed reported emissions. Points from an NDC document are that document's own inventory basis. The same year can appear more than once with different values; R3 keeps them side by side and never averages them.

derived.$reason: the document states a target of 90.4 MtCO₂e for 2030 on its own inventory, and the trend is measured on DS-35's. Two ledgers; the engine does not judge one against the other, just as it does not reconcile them on the divergence atlas.

ndc_assessment.vintage: First (I)NDC round, as assessed by WRI CAIT (2016). Not the latest submission.
ndc_assessment.summary: Cambodia has proposed a 27% reduction in emissions below BAU by 2030, as well as a LULUCF contribution of 4.7 tCO 2 e/ha/year. "Cambodia wishes to propose a GHG mitigation contribution for the period 2020 - 2030, conditional upon the availability of support from the international community, in particular in accordance with Article 4.3 of the UNFCCC. Significantly, despite Cambodia's status as an LDC, Cambodia is implementing actions in accordance with our sustainable development needs that also address climate change: (i)Energy industries, manufacturing industries, transport, and other sectors: Cambodia intends to undertake actions as listed in Table 1, the impact of which is expected to be a maximum reduction of 3,100 Gg CO 2 eq compared to baseline emissions of 11,600 Gg CO 2 eq by 2030. (ii) LULUCF: Cambodia intends to undertake voluntary and conditional actions to achieve the target of increasing forest cover to 60% of national land area by 2030. In absence of any actions the net sequestration from LULUCF is expected to 6 reduce to 7,897 GgCO 2 in 2030 compared to projected sequestration of 18,492 GgCO 2 in 2010." The INDC also includes a section on Adaptation.
ndc_assessment.ghg_target: 27% reduction in GHG emissions by 2030 compared to the BAU scenario, as well as a LULUCF contribution of 4.7 tCO2e/ha/year.
ndc_assessment.sectors: Energy Industries; Manufacturing Industries; Transport; Waste; Buildings; and Land Use, Land-Use Change and Forestry
ndc_assessment.$note: Third-party assessment of the first (I)NDC round. It is not merged into ndc.*, is not used by derive(), and does not appear on the dial as a target.

verdict.text: Cambodia pledges a 41.7% reduction by 2030 against 2030 BAU. A later submission, Cambodia’s NDC 3.0, was filed on 2025-08-08; it was read and refused, so no figure here comes from it. The document conditions its targets on international support but publishes no numeric split, so none is shown. 49 observed values are loaded from DS-02 (11), DS-06-NDC (1), DS-35 (35), DS-40 (2). For 2024 the sources disagree: DS-35 91.8 MtCO₂e, DS-02 47.5 MtCO₂e. They are on different inventory scopes and the engine does not reconcile them. No implementation gap is reported: the document states a target of 90.4 MtCO₂e for 2030 on its own inventory, and the trend is measured on DS-35's. Two ledgers; the engine does not judge one against the other, just as it does not reconcile them on the divergence atlas. It submitted BTR1 on 2024-12-31. 0 of 8 components have been confirmed in the document; the rest are unparsed, which is not a finding against the country. ND-GAIN scores it 42.4 for 2024. In the first NDC round, WRI's CAIT assessment recorded: 27% reduction in GHG emissions by 2030 compared to the BAU scenario, as well as a LULUCF contribution of 4.7 tCO2e/ha/year. It was classed conditional. That is a 2016 assessment of an earlier submission, not the target above. Projected warming for 2080-2099 against 1995-2014 ranges from +1.18°C under SSP1-2.6 to +3.81°C under SSP5-8.5. These are model runs, not observations.
